title: Sensex falls 500 points as profit-taking ends two-day rally; rupee edges up to 93.44
dek: Consumer durables, metal and IT stocks led the decline; gold and silver fell sharply on the MCX.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Indian shares fell on Wednesday, ending a two-day rally, as investors booked profits in consumer durables, metal, IT and auto stocks. The Sensex lost about 500 points, or 0.61 per cent, to close at about 82,030, and the Nifty 50 fell 159 points, or 0.63 per cent, to 25,227.95, according to reports; final Sensex figures in reports differ by under two points. Mid-cap stocks fell harder, with the Nifty Midcap 100 down 1.22 per cent.

Titan, Hindalco, Tata Steel, Maruti Suzuki and Sun Pharma were among the biggest losers, and the Nifty IT index fell about 1.2 per cent, while ITC, Bharti Airtel and PSU bank stocks gained, reports said. The fall came even as Nvidia's quarterly results, which beat forecasts, lifted chip stocks elsewhere in Asia.

The rupee edged up 7 paise to a provisional 93.44 against the dollar, helped by lower crude prices and foreign inflows, though a firm dollar and renewed US-Iran hostilities capped its gains, according to reports. It had closed at 93.51 on Tuesday, a seven-month high. Gold on the MCX fell 2.2 per cent to Rs 1,31,200 per 10 grams and silver 3.5 per cent, reports said.

Analysts quoted in reports saw 25,000 as the Nifty's key support level. Markets will watch Thursday's meeting of the US, Chinese and Russian leaders in Shenzhen for any signal on trade, Iran and Ukraine.
